summary: Runs an NVIDIA Flex particle-physics simulation for Actor COMPs and Force COMP fields, analogous to a world/solver that updates actor transforms using Flex-specific particle radius, cohesion, boundary, and iteration controls.

key_params.name: actors
key_params.note: Actor COMPs included in the Flex simulation

key_params.name: forces
key_params.note: Force COMPs used as Flex force fields

key_params.name: start
key_params.note: Initialize and begin stepping the simulation

key_params.name: rate
key_params.note: Simulation sample rate and timestep source

key_params.name: preroll
key_params.note: Run simulation before start to settle into an initial state

key_params.name: prerolltime
key_params.note: Simulation time to advance during pre-roll

key_params.name: alwayssim
key_params.note: Keep simulation stepping even when not otherwise demanded

key_params.name: boundmode
key_params.note: Use a bounding box SOP or individual planes as boundaries

key_concepts: NVIDIA Flex Solver COMP runs a Flex particle-physics simulation and updates referenced Actor COMP transforms as playback advances.
Referenced actors can live anywhere in the project, but cannot already be part of another Bullet or Flex Solver COMP.
Global forces are limited to Force COMP force-field behavior, and gravity applies to actors regardless of mass.
Initialize, Start, Play, rate, preroll, substeps, and iterations control simulation stepping and startup state.
Driver and GPU support is constrained; Derivative recommends NVIDIA 546.xx drivers and notes RTX 40 as the last supported card family.
common_gotchas: NVIDIA Flex Solver COMP is Windows-only.
Actors referenced by a Flex solver cannot already be referenced by another Solver COMP, including Bullet Solver COMP.
Only Force COMP force-field behavior is supported for Flex global forces.
Recent NVIDIA drivers can break some Flex features; Derivative notes 546.xx drivers as the recommended range and RTX 40 series as the last supported card family.
Pre-roll updates initial simulation state but can hide unstable setup until runtime if show-pre-roll and Info CHOP channels are not inspected.
Boundary planes do not need to be orthogonal, so misplaced planes can produce surprising containment behavior.
